title: What's New — Startup Recovery Hotfix
summary: PulseGuard v0.6.2 fixes a PowerShell parser error in the expanded hardware-stability card layout that could prevent v0.6.1 from opening after update. All v0.6.1 Evidence & Accuracy features remain included.

items.heading: Startup parser hotfix
items.detail: Fixed the malformed statement separator in the expanded 13-card stability-test layout that caused an Unexpected token n startup error in v0.6.1.

items.heading: Updater recovery preserved
items.detail: The launcher continues to run the updater before loading the main program, so an affected v0.6.1 installation can automatically receive this repair before the broken main script is parsed.

items.heading: Regression protection added
items.detail: Release tests now reject literal PowerShell newline/carriage-return escape artifacts when they appear between executable statements, preventing this exact source-generation mistake from shipping again.

items.heading: v0.6.1 diagnostics retained
items.detail: Evidence-first repair verification (including UNVERIFIED when proof is insufficient), exact-window WHEA/storage correlation, deeper hardware telemetry, driver provenance, storage/network/battery/latency diagnostics, PulseGuard video/audio tests, and conservative driver automation remain included. VRAM integrity still remains N/A without a trustworthy direct verifier, and no LatencyMon-style per-driver attribution is claimed.
